cases.solution: Use a supervised current-limited low-voltage cell or interactive measurement simulation. Vary load independently at two stable irradiances, measure U in parallel and I in the series load branch, control cell temperature and illumination drift and record actual independent settings/uncertainty. Do not call the supplied synthetic numbers a performed experiment. U·I in V·mA gives mW: high0,19.6,36,35,0;low0,9.6,16,10,0. Sampled maximum at.4V in both. Neither open-circuit I=0 nor short-circuit U=0 yields output power. Finite sampling does not prove the continuous optimum; measure more densely around.4–.5V under controls.

A second independent acquisition is required at two stable irradiances; reciting products alone does not satisfy it. Nominal high powers24,26,25mW;low12,12.4,11mW. High product bounds computed from positive endpoints:[.29·75,.31·85]=[21.75,26.35],[.39·60,.41·70]=[23.4,28.7],[.49·45,.51·55]=[22.05,28.05]mW. Low bounds[10.15,13.95],[10.14,14.76],[8.33,13.77]mW also overlap. Nominal.4V is not an exactly known MPP or firm ranking; repeat/resolve more finely.

solutions.fresh: Reviewer-generated third controlled acquisition U=.25,.35,.45V,I=60,50,30mA gives15,17.5,13.5mW and a sampled optimum.35V. Construct numeric U-I/P-U plots and bound continuous inference. Fresh data are analytic examples, not actual measurements.
